slots.title: Consumer confidence print due at 2 p.m. ET
slots.body:
At 2 p.m.
ET today, the U.S. gets August consumer confidence — the survey of how households feel about jobs and spending.

The estimate in the calendar is 90.3, down from 90.8 in July.

The same time slot has July new home sales (annualized pace, millions of units).

That release carries a 0.62 estimate versus 0.628 previously.

Both are flagged high and medium impact for the dollar data week.

slots.body:

slots.title: Aug. 24 US cash session recap
slots.body:
The Aug. 24 U.S. cash session split the main indexes.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 53,417.16 (+140.15, +0.3%).
The S&P 500 finished at 7,652.82 (−21.55, −0.3%).
The Nasdaq Composite ended at 25,980.19 (−200.26, −0.8%).
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,995.08 (−22.79, −0.8%).

Coverage described chip makers and other technology shares as a drag on the major benchmarks at the start of a busy week, with AI-related jitters and geopolitical headlines in the backdrop.
NVIDIA was among the most active names on the close at 208.48 (−2.9%), with Advanced Micro Devices at 456.75 (−3.5%), Taiwan Semiconductor at 410.12 (−2.1%), and Tesla at 348.95 (−3.8%).
Alphabet’s Class C shares bucked the tech tone at 344.59 (+0.8%).

Visa closed at 382.41 (+3.1%), with a session high of 383.43 matching the 52-week high in the quote data.
Costco rose 2.5% to 971.40.
Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Johnson & Johnson each finished about +1.0% to +1.3%, alongside a Consumer Defensive sector average near +1.8% — the strongest sector reading in the snapshot.

Energy was the weakest sector group at about −1.2%.
Brent crude settled at 90.42 (−1.9%).
The United States Oil Fund closed at 132.21 (−1.8%).
Exxon Mobil and Chevron finished at 164.05 (−0.6%) and 203.05 (−1.1%).
Communication Services averaged about +1.4%; Technology averaged about −1.0%; Industrials about −0.9%.

The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for July printed at −0.08, versus a 0.1 estimate and 0.06 prior in the economic calendar.
Later, 3-month and 6-month bill auction results were logged at 3.7% and 3.8%.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-08-21 in the data showed the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.50.
Gold futures (GCUSD) closed at 4,745.90 (+1.0%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was at 79,804.84 (+1.0%).
The Invesco dollar-bullish fund proxy (UUP) ticked up 0.2% to 27.96.
EUR/USD was flat at 1.17 in the feed.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose to 15.85 (+0.72, +4.8%) from a 15.13 prior close.
Overseas, the Hang Seng was down 1.9% at 25,517.33; the Nikkei 225 was off 0.6% at 65,142.88; the FTSE 100 was up 0.3% at 10,854.32.

No earnings entries were listed in the injected earnings calendar for this bundle.
The session’s economic and cross-asset prints sat alongside ongoing discussion of Treasury auction schedules and expanded buyback operations in the news flow.
